discovery: Photonic crystals and photonic band gaps: controlling the propagation and emission of light with periodic dielectric structures
subfield: Optics and photonics / wave physics in structured media
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently proposed that periodic dielectric structures can open a complete photonic band gap: Yablonovitch to inhibit spontaneous emission, John to localize light via disorder. Yablonovitch then realized the first three-dimensional photonic band-gap crystal (1991). Joannopoulos turned the concept into a predictive science, computing photonic band structures and designing defect cavities, waveguides and omnidirectional mirrors. Together they made light an electron-like wave in an engineered crystal, founding a new field. Its reach is exceptional: photonic-crystal fibers, nanolasers, slow light, integrated silicon photonics, and later topological photonics and synthetic gauge fields all rest on this foundation. The ideas also fed back into condensed matter, acoustics and quantum optics, where band-gap control of light–matter interaction now underpins cavity and waveguide QED. This is a rare case of a genuinely new physical concept that transformed both fundamental science and technology.
